entry.title: test(di): the Koin graph resolves, and the splash survives dark mode
entry.content:
test(di): the Koin graph resolves, and the splash survives dark mode

Both raised in review on #280.

**Koin 4.0.2 -> 4.2.2 had no automated coverage**, on the container that
constructs every repository and ViewModel. `git grep` finds no
`startKoin`, `checkModules` or `verify()` in any test source set: every
other test builds its subject directly or over a fake, so a binding the
new Koin resolved differently would first show up when an app launches,
and CI launches no activity.

`KoinGraphTest` starts the real graph — `sharedModule` plus
`jvmPlatformModule`, the same `sharedModule` the apps use — on the desktop
target and resolves all eleven repositories. They are named individually
rather than reflected over, so adding a repository without a binding fails
here instead of passing an empty loop, and the test was checked for
vacuity by asking it for an unbound type and confirming
`NoDefinitionFoundException`. This is the same move the stack already made
three times: `checkJniLibsArePackaged`, `checkNativeImageIsOneFile`, the
`afterEvaluate` predicate checks.

**The splash was verified on video rather than by racing a screenshot** —
it is too brief to catch, and it is the one surface Compose cannot reach,
with `core-splashscreen` moving two minors and no source change beside it.
`screenrecord` over a cold dark-mode launch, sampled at 6 fps: mean frame
luminance 18 -> 5 with no spike, so no white flash at the handoff, and the
splash frame shows the fox on the dark ground rather than the cream one —
`values-night/` still resolves.

Both recorded in the RESULTS.md entry for the stack.

entry.title: chore(deps): jna 5.19.1, sqlite-jdbc 3.53.4.0
entry.content:
chore(deps): jna 5.19.1, sqlite-jdbc 3.53.4.0

Alone in their own PR, because both ship native libraries and both are
reachable from `loopky`, which is shipped as a single `native-image`
binary. `native-image` does not fail when it cannot fold a JDK native
library in — it emits the library beside the executable and reports
success — so a bump here can quietly turn a one-file install into an
eight-file directory.

JNA is the more delicate of the two: the UniFFI bindings run on it, and
`com.sun.jna.Native` is hand-registered for JNI and **deliberately not**
for reflection in `cli/src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/`, because
a reflection entry makes `native-image` reconstruct an `Executable` for
every method the class declares and lands ten JDK dylibs beside the macOS
binary. That metadata is untouched here; if the bump needs it changed,
that is a finding to discuss rather than a patch to apply.

Verified locally as far as a machine without GraalVM can: `ciCheck` green,
and `:shared:jvmTest` — the only suite that loads the real libpubkycore —
passes 1408 tests, so JNA 5.19.1 is exercised against the FFI rather than
merely resolving. The CLI still answers `whoami --json` with exit 3.

**Not verified locally: `:cli:nativeCompile` and `checkNativeImageIsOneFile`.**
CI builds both rows on every PR that touches the catalog, and it has to be
both — last time a metadata change left Linux clean and macOS at eleven
files, and nobody saw it until the Mac row was built. A green Linux row is
not evidence here.

entry.content:
chore(deps): bring the catalog current

The routine half of #273 §2, no behaviour change intended: koin 4.0.2 ->
4.2.2, coil 3.0.4 -> 3.6.2, kotlinx-coroutines 1.10.2 -> 1.11.0,
kotlinx-serialization 1.9.0 -> 1.11.0, androidx-core 1.18.0 -> 1.19.0,
appcompat 1.7.1 -> 1.8.0, work 2.10.0 -> 2.11.2, credentials 1.5.0 ->
1.6.0, zxing 3.5.3 -> 3.5.4, graalvm-native 1.1.11 -> 1.1.12.

The lifecycle row was not routine. Bumping it to 2.11.0 broke
`:cli:installDist` outright — "Entry lib/lifecycle-common-jvm-2.11.0.jar
is a duplicate" — because the desktop classpath had ended up carrying both
`androidx.lifecycle` and `org.jetbrains.androidx.lifecycle`, two builds of
the same classes under one filename.

The fix is to stop using the JetBrains fork. Google now publishes
lifecycle as a multiplatform library itself: `androidx.lifecycle:
lifecycle-viewmodel:2.11.0` ships iosArm64 and iosSimulatorArm64 variants
alongside android and desktop, so the fork `:shared` was depending on for
its `commonMain` ViewModel has nothing left to add. Koin 4.2 had already
moved, which is what put both on the classpath at once. Navigation follows
for the same reason, and off its beta pin as well: `org.jetbrains.androidx.
navigation:navigation-compose:2.9.0-beta03` -> `androidx.navigation:
navigation-compose:2.10.0`.

That also settles the thing this stack was most careful about — the
multiplatform `ViewModel` all of `presentation/` extends and `:shared`
re-exports as `api` for iOS. It is now the one Google supports as Tier 1
KMP rather than a fork of it.

`ciCheck` green, `testAndroidHostTest` still 1373, and the CLI still
answers `whoami --json` with exit 3 and `not_signed_in` — the same
assertion CI makes on the shipped binary.

Raised in review on #279: the new §11 bullet said `androidx.lifecycle` is
Google's build and not the JetBrains fork, while this head's catalog says
`org.jetbrains.androidx.lifecycle`. The reviewer was right that it
contradicts the build, and right about why it matters — the sentence names
a real incident (`:cli:installDist` breaking when lifecycle went to

builds, in **#280**, and asserting here that they stay JetBrains with
Compose as the exception would be false one PR up. What actually happened
is that a paragraph describing the state after #280 landed in #279.

So this PR now claims only what it does: Compose moved, and Compose is the
only family that did — which is the inference the reviewer flagged as the
dangerous one, stated explicitly rather than left to be drawn. #280 adds

entry.title: refactor(build): AndroidX Compose, off the Compose Multiplatform alphas
entry.content:
refactor(build): AndroidX Compose, off the Compose Multiplatform alphas

Compose Multiplatform was buying nothing here. `:shared` contains no
Compose at all, iOS is SwiftUI by settled decision, and `:androidApp`
imports only `androidx.compose.*` — not one `org.jetbrains.compose.*`
import across 123 files, because the JetBrains artifacts publish under the
AndroidX package namespace. So this swaps coordinates, not code.

What it buys is leaving the alpha channel. `material3` was pinned at
`1.10.0-alpha05` because that is where Material 3 Expressive lived, and
the issue framed the pin as a standing decision to re-take. It isn't one
any more: AndroidX material3 **1.4.0 is stable** and ships
`ShortNavigationBar` and `WideNavigationRail`, which are Loopky's entire
Expressive surface. `LoadingIndicator` looked like a third until it turned
out to be a parameter named `showLoadingIndicator`.

They are stable enough that `ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi` is now
**internal**, so `LoopkyNavRail`'s opt-in had to go — the one source
change in this commit, and the one place the swap was not purely
mechanical.

One BOM (`androidx.compose:compose-bom:2026.08.00`) replaces four version
refs and pins the family to a set Google released together: foundation and
runtime 1.12.0, material3 1.4.0, material3-adaptive 1.3.0,
material-icons-extended 1.7.8. `components-resources` is dropped outright
— nothing referenced `Res.*`.

This had to follow the AGP 9 flip rather than precede it: AndroidX Compose
1.12 requires AGP 9.1+ and `compileSdk 37`, and refuses to build below
either. `compileSdk` moves to 37 here for that reason; `targetSdk` stays
36, which already meets Play's 31 Aug 2026 floor.

`navigationCompose` comes off its `2.9.0-beta03` pin to 2.9.2, and stays
the JetBrains build along with `androidx-lifecycle` — those are the two
that must not move, since `:shared` re-exports the multiplatform
`ViewModel` as `api` for iOS. Checked rather than assumed: the JetBrains
lifecycle and navigation modules redirect to their AndroidX counterparts
on the Android target, everything converges on lifecycle 2.10.0, and
`checkDebugDuplicateClasses` passes.

entry.title: perf(ios): incremental klib compilation, on its own and written down
entry.content:
perf(ios): incremental klib compilation, on its own and written down

Split out of the AGP/Gradle/Kotlin commit on review of #278. The point
stands: that commit justifies four rejected version choices and never
mentioned a fourth moving part, so the flag read as accidental — and a
three-way toolchain jump is exactly the commit someone bisects later,
where an unrelated Kotlin/Native flag is the confounder CLAUDE.md's
atomic-commit rule exists to prevent.

What it buys: Kotlin/Native's documented lever for the iOS
edit-build-drive loop, which is where that target spends its time.

What it costs, and why it needs a paper trail rather than a green matrix:
it is **Beta and off by default upstream**, so it is a real behaviour
change, and **no CI job can exercise it** — every runner is fresh, so klib
incrementality is structurally a no-op there. Its failure mode is a stale
klib surviving a source change, which surfaces as a local iOS build that
disagrees with the source and nothing reporting why.

So it is recorded where someone hits it: a line in CLAUDE.md beside the
iOS build guidance saying to turn this off first if a build looks stale,
rather than only a comment in `gradle.properties` that nobody reads until
they already suspect the build system.

entry.title: chore(build): AGP 9.3.1, Gradle 9.6.1, Kotlin 2.4.20
entry.content:
chore(build): AGP 9.3.1, Gradle 9.6.1, Kotlin 2.4.20

The flip #273 was aiming at. With `:androidApp` off KMP and `:shared` on
`com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library`, nothing here needs
`android.newDsl=false` — the opt-out with the AGP 10.0 expiry date is
never set, which was the point of the exercise.

AGP **9.3.1** rather than the 9.4.0 the issue names: KGP 2.4.20 publishes
support up to AGP 9.3.1, and 9.4.0 sits outside every published Kotlin
compatibility row. Gradle **9.6.1** rather than the issue's 9.1.0, which
is AGP 9.0's floor — AGP 9.3 requires 9.5.0, and 9.3.0 exactly is worth
avoiding (gradle#36428 breaks cross-project dependency manipulation there,
which is what the root's `subprojects { dependencies { … } }` does).

The wrapper and AGP had to move in one commit rather than two. AGP 8.13.2
cannot run on Gradle 9.6.0+ at all — it relies on
`org.gradle.api.problems.internal.InternalProblems`, removed there — and
AGP 9.3 needs Gradle >= 9.5, so neither can lead. `gradle-wrapper.properties`
was edited directly and the wrapper regenerated once the build came up.

`org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` and the `jvmTarget` override come out of
`:androidApp`: `android.builtInKotlin` defaults true here, and built-in
Kotlin takes its jvmTarget from `android.compileOptions.targetCompatibility`,
which is already JVM 11. AGP 9 lists that plugin as incompatible with the
new DSL, so this is the removal it was placed for two commits ago.
`android.nonTransitiveRClass` and `android.useAndroidX` are AGP 9 defaults
and go with it.

detekt 1.23.8 survives all three moves, so the conditional detekt 2
migration is not needed. Its published table stops at Gradle 8.12.1 /
Kotlin 2.0.21 / AGP 8.8.1 and it is EOL, so this was checked rather than
assumed: `detektAll` passes, and a deliberately misnamed class is still
reported, i.e. it is analysing rather than quietly finding nothing.

`ciCheck` green. `testAndroidHostTest` still 1373 tests.

entry.title: fix(build): run the jniLibs assertion where CI can see it
entry.content:
fix(build): run the jniLibs assertion where CI can see it

Raised in review on #277, and the diagnosis was right: the guard added
because "an AAR built without them is a valid AAR, and the first sign of a
missing one is an FFI call failing on a device long after CI went green"
was itself only reachable from `ciCheck`. #239's shape exactly — the check
exists, the failure is silent, and nothing on the PR runs it.

Wired as `finalizedBy` on `bundleAndroidMainAar`, the reviewer's preferred
option and the same shape as `:cli:nativeCompile`/`checkNativeImageIsOneFile`,
so the assertion rides along with any build that produces an AAR rather
than only with workflows that remember to ask.

**One correction to the premise, and it is why a CI step is here too.**
`:androidApp:assembleDebug` does *not* reach the finalizer: AGP consumes
this module's intermediate artifacts, not the packaged AAR
(`./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug --dry-run` never mentions
`bundleAndroidMainAar`). So `finalizedBy` alone would have run the check
strictly *less* often than before. `:shared:assembleAndroidMain` is what
produces an AAR, so that is what `ciCheck` and the `test-build` job now
ask for, and the comment at both ends says why.

Also from the same review, both LOW:

- The ABI extraction computed a `substringAfterLast` and discarded it via
  `let { _ -> }`, then re-read the outer receiver. Same behaviour in one
  clause. Re-verified by adding a bogus ABI and watching the finalizer
  fail, rather than by reading it.
- Dropped the now-unused `androidLibrary` catalog entry. Nothing referenced
  `com.android.library` once `:shared` moved to `androidKmpLibrary`.

entry.title: refactor(build): :shared onto com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library
entry.content:
refactor(build): :shared onto com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library

The reason #273 exists. AGP 9 makes the new DSL the default and lists
`org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform` beside `com.android.library` in one
subproject as incompatible with it; `android.newDsl=false` buys time and
is removed in AGP 10.0. This is the replacement Google points at, and it
is applied here at AGP 8.13 — the plugin has existed since 8.10 — so the
structural change is verified before the AGP 9 flip moves anything else.

The `android {}` block moves inside `kotlin {}` and absorbs what the
bottom-level `android {}` held. `compileOptions` is deleted rather than
translated: Java compilation is off unless `withJava()`, and there is no
`.java` here. `androidResources` stays off; there is no `res/`.

Three things that fail silently, so all three are asserted rather than
trusted:

**The hierarchy group stops matching.** `withAndroidTarget()` selects
`KotlinAndroidTarget`; this plugin creates a different target type, so the
custom `jvmShared` group is built *without* the Android target in it,
`androidMain` falls back to `commonMain`, and the generated
`uniffi.pubkycore` bindings disappear from the Android compile. That is
KT-80409, still open, and it reproduces here — swapping the predicate back
fires the new `afterEvaluate` check. The fix is
`withCompilations { it is KotlinMultiplatformAndroidCompilation }`, which
is published API on both sides.

**Host tests are opt-in.** AGP only warns about a missing `withHostTest`
when a `src/androidHostTest` directory exists, and there is none —
`commonTest` is what runs on this target. Without the opt-in the Android
test run just disappears. With it, `testAndroidHostTest` reports 1373
tests in 105 classes, matching the `testDebugUnitTest` baseline recorded
at the bottom of this stack exactly, so `isReturnDefaultValues` survived
the move.

**jniLibs are packaged by convention, not by declaration.** They are —
all four `libpubkycore.so` land in `shared.aar` under `jni/<abi>/` — but
nothing in the build says so, and an AAR built without them is a valid
AAR whose first symptom is an FFI call failing on a device. So
`checkJniLibsArePackaged` asserts it and is wired into `ciCheck`, in the
same spirit as `:cli:checkNativeImageIsOneFile`.

Renames that follow: source set `androidUnitTest` -> `androidHostTest`
(detekt's source list and its four excludes), task
`:shared:testDebugUnitTest` -> `:shared:testAndroidHostTest` (`ciCheck`,
ci.yml, Architecture.md). `:cli`'s `shared-jvm.jar` lookup is unchanged in
outcome but now says so when it misses, since this plugin forces
`kotlin.publishJvmEnvironmentAttribute` on and a silent `first {}` failure
there would read as a native-row bug.

refactor(build): :composeApp becomes :androidApp, a plain Android module

AGP 9 forbids the shape this module had (#273). The release notes are
explicit: "The new KMP integration does not support using KMP and the
Android Application plugin in the same Gradle subproject" — and unlike
`:shared`, there is no `com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.*` plugin for an
application to migrate onto. The app has to stop being a KMP module.

That turned out to cost nothing, because it was never really one. Only
`src/androidMain/` existed on disk; there was no `commonMain` and no test
source set at all, so `:composeApp:testDebugUnitTest` was running zero
tests. The single `composeResources/` entry was the project template's
unused `compose-multiplatform.xml`, and nothing referenced `Res.*`. So
the KMP scaffolding is deleted rather than ported: `src/androidMain` ->
`src/main`, and the three source-set dependency lists collapse into one
`dependencies {}` block.

Renamed to `:androidApp` in the same commit, matching JetBrains' new
default KMP structure and retiring the line CLAUDE.md had to carry
explaining that `composeApp` was Android-only despite its name.

`org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` is applied temporarily: AGP 8.13 has no
built-in Kotlin, and AGP 9 lists that plugin as incompatible with the new
DSL. Both it and the `jvmTarget` override come out at the AGP 9 flip,
where `android.builtInKotlin` defaults true.

Two things verified rather than assumed. `compose.materialIconsExtended`
still resolves — the `compose` accessor comes from `org.jetbrains.compose`,
which registers on any project, not only a KMP one. And detekt still lints
all 123 files: they moved to `src/main/kotlin`, which the root's explicit
`source` list already carries for `:cli`. That list's own comment warns
that a missing entry is silently unlinted, so it was proved with a
deliberate violation rather than inferred from a green run.

`ciCheck` green; the APK still carries libpubkycore.so for all four ABIs.
